articles.title: Infantino proposes an ‘independent external review’ of Fifa governance
articles.summary: President writes to council and member nations. Infantino says he is ‘fully committed to leading Fifa’ The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has agreed to commission an independent governance review after coming under mounting pressure to do so in the wake of the World Cup sale debacle.
body: The Guardian revealed last month that several members of the Fifa council had been lobbying for an external review of both the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise sell-off and the Folarin Balogun controversy – with the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt, increasing the pressure last week by writing to Infantino demanding the release of all documents relating to both issues.

Infantino opted not to engage with the disgruntled members of the council, but in a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations he has indicated his willingness to submit to external scrutiny for the first time.
In addition, Infantino also invited proposals to review Fifa’s internal decision-making processes, which he said would be discussed at the next Fifa council meeting in Zurich on 15 October.

“First, I will ask the council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements,” Infantino wrote.

articles.title: Come back soon Premier League, the endlessly moreish mega-product | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Brighton have impressed in a goal-laden start to the season, in a league that remains a brutally strong attraction. Get ready for the dopamine crash. And this one really is a proper autumn nosedive. The past 17 days up to and including Sunday’s cut-off gave us 30 Premier League games and 79 goals.
body: Are your pathways stimulated? Are the neural connectors flickering? Well get ready for cold turkey, for 19 blank days of shivers and shakes until the Premier League show resumes in October. Maybe it really is time to buy one of those powders off the internet.

The international break will provide its own intrigue. There will be discussions about whether Thomas Tuchel is or isn’t responsible for the inherited cultural weaknesses of English football. There will be rage at Tuchel’s inability to coach the players to keep the ball as never before via his few short hours on the training pitch. And yet more rage at the real issues, basically the fact he continues to be German and looks like a scurvy-ridden Napoleonic naval commander powered solely by ship’s biscuits and morphine.

articles.title: Veronica Burton has been essential to Valkyries' success. Will she deliver in the playoffs?
articles.summary: Golden State point guard Veronica Burton improved her shooting this year after a 2025 breakthrough. Now the Valkyries may need her to create more offense in the postseason.
body: Veronica Burton kept deferring. She had hoisted 500 shots every day that week, with her dad Steve rebounding during their customary early-morning workouts, but then young Veronica became consumed with setting up her teammates in the first game of an AAU doubleheader.

Steve Burton told Veronica, then 13 or 14, to get in the car so they could drive home. They were going to skip the second game, because what was the point of all that practice if Veronica was going to be so passive?

"She started crying," Steve Burton recalled in a phone interview Monday. "She promised to take the shots she needed to take, so we turned around. She wiped away her tears, went back in the gym and scored 40. And they won."

This speaks to the push-and-pull Veronica Burton still faces now, on a much bigger stage, as the Golden State Valkyries prepare for the WNBA playoffs. They enter Tuesday night's game in Portland at 31-11, the league's second-best record, and eye Sunday's postseason opener with realistic ambitions of chasing the championship in only their second year of existence.

articles.title: Ten lessons from Jakob Ingebrigtsen, one of the world’s most beguiling athletes
articles.summary: Norwegian is meticulous in his training regime – ‘if there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly’ On a snowy Norwegian morning in January, Jakob Ingebrigtsen was on his treadmill, shooting the breeze about his running philosophy before our more formal interview.
body: In recent weeks, the 26‑year‑old has added to his legacy with a European 5,000m gold, the World Ultimate 5,000m title and a world road silver medal despite achilles surgery in February and a flu that lingered through May and June. So now seems as good a time as any.

Some of Ingebrigtsen’s opinions were a little hardcore. Others reiterated basic truths. But whether you are a runner or not, there are certainly some life lessons from one of the most beguiling athletes around.

Ingebrigtsen runs a lot, around 175-180km in a typical week. Apart from his family, that is his sole focus. “I prioritise the absolute crucial,” he says. “That is to wake up, to eat, to train.” It is, he concedes, not a life most would enjoy. “A lot of people could never be in my shoes, having my responsibility. They just wouldn’t handle it. But that’s how I want to be. If there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly.”
“If you have a day off, you lose 20-25km of running,” he says. Counterintuitively, perhaps, he believes the risk of injury goes up too and tries to run even when he is moderately poorly.

articles.title: Harry Brook says Brydon Carse ‘just needs time away from the international scene’
articles.summary: Bowler ‘is working on a few things’ England v Sri Lanka ODIs come a year before World Cup. Harry Brook is hopeful that Brydon Carse will break back into his England white-ball teams once the fast bowler is clear of his disciplinary proceedings, describing him as a “very good mate” who is “working…
body: Carse discovered recently he will not face a criminal charge for the late-night incident in Derby last month that led to him being briefly handcuffed. But while technically available for selection, the 31‑year‑old has not featured in England’s squads since that night as he awaits the outcome of an investigation by the Cricket Regulator.

Asked before Tuesday’s first one‑day international against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street about the prospect of Carse returning down the line, Brook, England’s white-ball captain, replied: “He’s a very good cricketer. He’s been bowling extremely well for Durham. When his time for selection is up, that will be a debate.

“I’m very good mates with Carsey. I’ve spoken a lot with him. Those conversations are private. I think he just needs time away from the international scene. He’s working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he’ll be ready at some point in the future.”

More broadly, Brook believes the call for greater off-field professionalism has permeated through the England squads, both from Brendon McCullum, the white-ball head coach, and Stephen Fleming ahead of his new role with the Test side.

articles.title: Infantino says he is open to talks over Fifa reform
articles.summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates. shifting tone as he seeks support to stay on.
body: In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".
Before a meeting of the Council next month, Infantino says he is also suggesting a consultation on "how Fifa's decision-making can be further strengthened".
This would include proposals on the role of the president, as well as "practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

articles.title: McLaren predict four-way battle for Baku win after confirming more upgrades
articles.summary: McLaren have confirmed they will bring more upgrades to this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where they are expecting a four-way battle for victory with Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull.
body: After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.
McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.
"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

articles.title: Spurs bottom of PL but more than £300m spent - where do they go from here?
articles.summary: This time it was supposed to be different. After multiple false dawns for Tottenham Hotspur, the club had a manager with proven Premier League experience, and had handed him a £300m+ war chest - easily the biggest in its entire history.
body: Instead, Spurs find themselves bottom of the table after five games for the first time in 18 years, with their only goals a pair of consolation strikes on another dismal afternoon against Aston Villa at the weekend.

Things aren't quite as bad as the table suggests and had Tottenham taken any of a number of presentable first-half chances against Villa, they would have gone into the three-week international break silencing some of the noise around the club.
But instead, two points from five games and such a dismal record in front of goal has kept the spotlight firmly on them.

Though it is only five games, their struggles to find consistency have extended into a third consecutive season. Tottenham have now picked up just 18 points in 2026 and, since the start of 2024/25, still one fewer than a West Ham side who were relegated at the end of last season.

articles.title: Being run over by pitch roller was 'terrifying' - Townsend
articles.summary: Townsend says he was lucky to only escape from under the roller with a few "bumps and bruises".
body: Former England winger Andros Townsend has described the moment he was run over by a pitch roller in Thailand as "terrifying".

The 35‑year‑old former Tottenham, Luton and Crystal Palace forward, now with PT Prachuap in Thai League 1, was warming up for a match in Pattani on Saturday when a member of staff appeared to lose control of a heavy pitch roller.
Townsend's left leg briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he was unhurt. He came off the bench late on in a 3-0 win.
"Every time I see it, I'm cringing, I'm in disbelief," he said.

articles.title: Israel FA accuses Hallgrimsson of 'ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity'
articles.summary: The Israel FA accuse Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity" in comments made last week.
body: During his squad announcement for the upcoming Nations League games which include two fixtures against Israel on 27 September and 4 October, Hallgrimsson said: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel," when the subject of keeping his players focused on the games was raised.

On Monday, Israel's football body hit back on those comments on social media, saying: "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

"Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

The Football Association of Ireland has not responded to the Israel FA's comments, with a protest also taking place at the Republic of Ireland team's hotel on Monday evening as pressure to boycott the fixtures continues to build.
